changed.title: The sole binary-formula density strictly between seven sixteenths and one half has a unique five-variable form
changed.statement:
∀ n : ℕ,
  let W := Fin n → Bool
  let Lit := Fin n × Bool
  let F := Finset (Lit × Lit)
  let sat := fun (C : F) (w : W) => decide (∀ c ∈ C,
    w c.1.1 ≠ c.1.2 ∨ w c.2.1 ≠ c.2.2)
  let Q := 2 ^ n
  ∀ A : F,
    let N := (Finset.univ.filter (fun z => sat A z = true)).card
    let cert := ∀ x : W, sat A x = true →
      ∃ T : Finset (Fin n), T.card ≤ 2 ∧
        ∀ y : W, (∀ i ∈ T, y i = x i) → sat A y = true
    let half := ∃ (j : Fin n) (v : Bool), ∀ p : W, p j = v → sat A p = true
    let shape := ∃ (sites : Fin 5 → Fin n) (signs : Fin 5 → Bool),
      Function.Injective sites ∧ ∀ word : W,
        let mark := fun k : Fin 5 => word (sites k) = signs k
        sat A word = decide (¬(mark 0 ∧ (mark 1 ∨ mark 2)) ∧ ¬(mark 3 ∧ mark 4))
    (Q ≤ 2 * N → half ∨ cert) ∧ (2 * N = Q → cert) ∧
      ((7 * Q < 16 * N ∧ 2 * N < Q) ↔ shape) ∧
      (shape → 32 * N = 15 * Q)
changed.unlocks: identifies the only hidden binary-clause density strictly between seven sixteenths and one half and classifies its predicates
changed.context: Unary exclusions and conflicting forbidden pairs give half cores with certificates of size two. Otherwise orient every bit consistently and count independent sets. With matching number at most one get a star or triangle. Beside two matched edges, a third gives three disjoint edges (27/64), a four-vertex path (1/2), or a two-edge path and separate edge (15/32). Every passing word of the four-vertex path has a two-bit certificate, and the last graph has three-bit certificates. Any further clause cutting a core loses at least 1/16 or 1/32 respectively.

changed.title: Known moment estimate rebuilt for signed first-order Walsh coefficients on a subset of the binary cube
changed.statement:
∀ (k m : ℕ), 0 < m →
  let N := 2^k
  ∀ (S : Finset (Fin N)) (b : Fin N → Bool),
    let v := fun (j : Fin k) =>
      ∑ x ∈ S, if xor (b x) (x.val.testBit j.val) then (-1 : ℝ) else 1
    let energy := ∑ j : Fin k, (v j)^2
    energy^m ≤ (N : ℝ) * (S.card : ℝ)^(2*m-1) * (∏ j ∈ Finset.range m, (2*(j:ℝ)+1))
changed.unlocks: bounds the signed first-level Walsh energy of a subset using its density and an explicit even moment
changed.context: L is the signed sum over S of the linear form with coefficients v. Apply the finite power-mean bound at exponent 2m, then extend the even-power sum to the whole cube. In its expansion only tuples with every index repeated evenly survive. Each admits a pairing of equal indices and has nonnegative coefficient. Each pairing sums to L^m, and there are (2m-1)!! pairings. Cancel L^m when positive. Zero energy is immediate.

changed.title: One-a-side promise: the 3 by 4 bipartite graph with mask 363 has a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit of at most 7 gates
changed.statement: PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun (u : Fin 3) (v : Fin 4) => (363 : ℕ).testBit (4 * u.val + v.val)) 7
changed.unlocks: the AND/OR cost of 3 by 4 graphs off the square, where the checked twin merge sends square graphs, for the silent-line work
changed.sketch: A search unit. We hold a circuit of 8 AND/OR gates for this graph that shares nothing; we hold none of 7; this is a search. Our count of unread rows and columns gives a floor of 6 (on paper), a gap of 2. The checked twin merge reduces a square graph to a rectangular quotient, and we hold no table off the square beyond 2 by 3. Answer with a gate list (AND or OR, each reading at most two wires; wires 0 to 2 left, 3 to 6 right, gate j writes wire 7 + j, each gate reading only earlier wires) and its output wire, judged on all 12 inputs with one vertex on each side.

changed.title: Exact tree-like resolution leaf cost after replacing binary clauses by private implication chains
changed.statement:
∀ (n m : ℕ) (src dst : Fin m → Fin n × Bool) (len : Fin m → ℕ),
  (∀ e, 0 < len e ∧ (src e).1 ≠ (dst e).1) →
  let V := Fin n ⊕ (Fin m × ℕ)
  let lit := fun (e : Fin m) (j : ℕ) =>
    if j = 0 then ((Sum.inl (src e).1 : V), (src e).2)
    else if j = len e then ((Sum.inl (dst e).1 : V), (dst e).2)
    else ((Sum.inr (e,j) : V), true)
  let step := fun (e : Fin m) (j : ℕ) =>
    ({((lit e j).1, !(lit e j).2), lit e (j+1)} : PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause V)
  let big : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause V) := {C | ∃ e j, j < len e ∧ C = step e j}
  let base := fun clauseIndex : Fin m =>
    ({((Sum.inl (src clauseIndex).1 : V), !(src clauseIndex).2), ((Sum.inl (dst clauseIndex).1 : V), (dst clauseIndex).2)} :
      PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause V)
  Function.Injective base →
  let tree := fun (leaf : PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause V → ℕ → Prop) (K : ℕ) =>
    ∃ (nodes inner : Finset (List Bool)) (line : List Bool → PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause V)
      (cost : List Bool → ℕ), [] ∈ nodes ∧ inner ⊆ nodes ∧ line [] = ∅ ∧
      (nodes \ inner).sum cost ≤ K ∧
      (∀ p ∈ nodes, p ∉ inner → leaf (line p) (cost p)) ∧
      (∀ (p : List Bool) (a : Bool), p ++ [a] ∈ nodes → p ∈ inner) ∧
      ∀ p ∈ inner, p ++ [false] ∈ nodes ∧ p ++ [true] ∈ nodes ∧
        PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.IsResolvent (line (p ++ [false])) (line (p ++ [true])) (line p)
  ∀ K : ℕ,
    tree (fun C charge => C ∈ big ∧ charge = 1) K ↔
    tree (fun D price => ∃ idx, D = base idx ∧ price = len idx) K
changed.unlocks: computes the independent tree leaf cost under private path substitution using weighted original leaf occurrences
changed.context: At each original leaf resolve the chain to recover that clause with t_e leaves. In reverse pick one uniformly random breakpoint in each chain. Map the private literals on the two sides to the two endpoint literals. All links except the breakpoint become tautologies. Project the resolution tree by pruning tautologies and keeping subclauses. Each leaf on chain e survives as a candidate with probability 1/t_e and carries weight t_e, so some projected tree has weight at most the original leaf count.

changed.title: Low total query degree on a successful transcript forces many errors nearby for a list of translated predictions
changed.statement:
∀ (m r L d : Nat), 0 < L →
  let V := Fin m × Fin r
  let W := V → Bool
  let deg := fun (b : Nat) (f : W → Bool) =>
    ∃ terms : Finset (Finset V), (∀ mon ∈ terms, mon.card ≤ b) ∧
      ∀ input, f input = (((terms.filter (fun mon => ∀ j ∈ mon, input j = true)).card % 2) == 1)
  let t := m/L
  let F := Fin t → Bool
  let run := fun (ask : Nat → Nat → W → Bool) (n : Nat) (x : W) =>
    (List.range n).foldl (fun h pos => h + ((ask pos h x).toNat <<< pos)) 0
  ∀ (ask : Nat → Nat → W → Bool) (leaf : Nat → Fin L → Fin m → Fin r → Bool) (base : W),
    let path := run ask d base
    (∃ a : Fin L, ∀ i, (fun v => base (i,v)) ≠ leaf path a i) →
    ∀ B : Fin d → Nat, (∀ u, deg (B u) (ask u.val (run ask u.val base))) →
    ∃ (driver : V → Option (Fin t)) (embed : F → W),
      (∀ flags site, embed flags site = xor (base site) ((driver site).elim false flags)) ∧
      Function.Injective embed ∧
      (∀ flags : F, (∃ z, flags z = true) → ∀ a : Fin L, ∃ i,
        (fun v => embed flags (i,v)) = leaf path a i) ∧
      2^(t - ∑ u : Fin d, B u) ≤ 1 +
        ((Finset.univ : Finset F).filter (fun active =>
          (∃ z, active z = true) ∧ run ask d (embed active) = path)).card
changed.unlocks: Counts unavoidable errors on a single reached list using the degrees of its actual queries.
changed.context: Take t disjoint groups of L coordinates. On a switch, set the assigned coordinate of every candidate to its forbidden symbol. Each group changes at least one raw bit since one candidate was valid at the base. Switches are disjoint, hence injective. The indicator of the base path is a product of its answer literals and has degree at most D on this cube. It is one at zero. A nonzero Boolean polynomial of degree D on t bits has at least 2^max(t-D,0) nonzeros. All the other nonzeros are errors.
